cues: The polymerase chain reaction, invented by Kary Mullis in nineteen eighty three, copies one chosen stretch of DNA millions of times, in a tube, with no cell at all.
The tube holds the DNA, two short primers that flank the target, the four nucleotides, and a heat proof polymerase, Taq, from a hot spring bacterium.
